        "Non-head lines were previously discarded in this parser. In decompose mode, the new path expands parallel header/buffer/object arrays, copies headers and buffers each child. The finalizer destroys buffers, frees copied headers and frees arrays; child object pointers are borrowed and are not freed by that loop. The allocator zeroes object data before initialization, supporting initially zero counts/pointers. The three array allocations have a common failure guard; buffer writes separately reject invalid arguments.",
        "After head parsing, the patch closes the head decomposition stream before replaying children. Actual draft callbacks increment/decrement decompose_init_count, so a child must start at top level rather than reuse the head attachment. It is not a promise to retain every related part as an attachment.",
        "The original FAIL label moves after the replay block. Errors in head parsing or child output jump past the normal close steps and restore output callbacks; the test does not inject those failures. Accepted code later uses ScopeExit to restore output callbacks and early error returns, while the same normal head-close/child-replay order remains. This is a static cleanup-boundary observation, not a demonstrated stream leak, crash or complete failure-recovery guarantee.",
